name: range_day_band_fade_v132
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: NIFTY spends roughly 40% of trading sessions in a rotational, non-trending state — the index oscillates within a 60-100 spot point range as institutional participants wait for catalysts and market makers dominate order flow. On these range days, retail and algorithmic momentum chasers push NIFTY toward the edges of its intraday range, creating 15-30 spot point overextensions that reliably snap back toward the session's fair value. This strategy identifies confirmed range days using ADX as a trend-absence filter on NIFTY spot, then waits for price to stretch toward the Bollinger Band extremes — indicating a statistical overextension within the rotational structure. The critical distinction from generic VWAP mean-reversion is the ADX gating: this strategy REFUSES to trade on trending days, where band-touch entries become trend-continuation traps. On NIFTY specifically, range days exhibit a characteristic pattern where the first 45-60 minutes establish the day's range boundaries, and subsequent moves toward those boundaries fade with high reliability because there is no institutional directional flow to sustain a breakout. At 5-second resolution, we detect the exact bar where NIFTY touches the Bollinger Band boundary during a confirmed range regime and shows a reversal candle, entering 10-30 seconds before traders on 1-minute charts see a completed reversal bar. We capture 5-10 ATM option points as price reverts toward the session midpoint, exiting well before full VWAP reversion because range-day reversions are shallow and contested by other mean-reversion participants.

indicators.name: adx_168
indicators.purpose: Range-day confirmation filter computed over 14 minutes of 5-second bars. The original used ADX(14) on 1-min bars = 14 minutes of price action, which captures the intraday trend strength over a window that's long enough to distinguish genuine directional flow from noise but short enough to adapt when a range day transitions to a trend day. On NIFTY, ADX below 18 over 14 minutes reliably indicates rotational tape — the index is oscillating without directional commitment. We use 168 bars (14 minutes at 5s) rather than a naive 12x scaling to 168 because the 14-minute window is the meaningful unit: it's roughly the duration of one NIFTY intraday swing leg on a range day (the index takes 10-20 minutes to travel from mid-range to boundary and back). A shorter window would produce noisy ADX readings from individual 5s bar volatility; a longer window would be too slow to detect when a range day is breaking into a trend.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumsum(close * volume) / cumsum(volume) from session open
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP as the rotational fair-value anchor. On range days, NIFTY orbits VWAP tightly — the session's volume-weighted midpoint acts as the gravitational center that price reverts toward after each overextension. VWAP is cumulative and bar-size independent, so no lookback scaling is needed.

indicators.name: vwap_slope_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute VWAP slope as a flat-tape confirmation filter. The original used vwap_slope_10 on 1-min bars = 10 minutes of VWAP drift. On range days, VWAP should be essentially flat — drifting less than 5-8 spot points over 10 minutes. If VWAP is trending (slope > threshold), the market is not truly rotational and band-touch fades will be run over by directional flow. The 10-minute window (120 bars at 5s) matches the original's intent: long enough to smooth out micro-fluctuations in VWAP but short enough to detect when directional flow begins mid-session.

indicators.name: bb_mid_240
indicators.purpose: 20-minute SMA as the Bollinger Band center. The original used SMA(20) on 1-min bars = 20-minute moving average. On NIFTY at 5s, 240 bars = 20 minutes. This lookback is appropriate for range-day band fading because NIFTY's rotational swings on range days have a half-period of roughly 15-25 minutes — price takes about that long to move from one range boundary to the other. A 20-minute SMA sits at the midpoint of these oscillations, making it the natural mean-reversion target. A shorter lookback (e.g., 10 minutes) would chase price too closely; a longer one (e.g., 40 minutes) would lag behind when the range shifts.

indicators.name: bb_upper_240
indicators.purpose: Upper Bollinger Band at 2.2 standard deviations. The 2.2x multiplier (rather than the standard 2.0) is retained from the original because it sets a wider band specifically for range-day trading — on range days, price touches the 2.0 BB frequently during normal oscillation, but 2.2 BB touches indicate genuine overextension beyond the rotational equilibrium. On NIFTY range days with a 60-100 spot point range, the 2.2 BB on a 20-minute window sits approximately 25-40 spot points from the midline, capturing the extreme edges of the rotation.

indicators.name: bb_lower_240
indicators.purpose: Lower Bollinger Band at 2.2 standard deviations. Mirror of bb_upper_240 for detecting downside overextension within the range-day rotation.

indicators.name: rsi_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute RSI as the oscillator confirmation. The original used MFI(5) on 1-min bars — a volume-weighted RSI over 5 minutes. On NIFTY index, volume-weighting adds noise because aggregated index volume doesn't cleanly reflect directional conviction the way individual stock volume does. Plain RSI over 60 bars (5 minutes at 5s) preserves the original's intent — detecting overbought/oversold conditions at the range boundary — without the volume noise. The 5-minute window is chosen because it captures one complete micro-swing within the range day: if price has been moving in one direction for 5 minutes and RSI is extreme, the swing is mature and ripe for reversal.

indicators.name: atr_168
indicators.purpose: 14-minute ATR used for normalizing the VWAP slope threshold. On NIFTY, a flat-tape VWAP slope should be less than 8% of the prevailing ATR — this adapts the flatness threshold to the day's actual volatility rather than using a fixed number. Matches the original's use of ATR(14) on 1-min bars for the same normalization purpose.

conditions: adx_168 < 18 (NIFTY is in confirmed range-day regime — no directional trend over the past 14 minutes of 5s bars)
ABS(vwap_slope_120) < 0.08 * atr_168 (VWAP is flat — the session midpoint is not drifting, confirming true rotation rather than a slow grind)
close <= bb_lower_240 OR close within 3 spot points of bb_lower_240 (NIFTY has stretched to the lower edge of the 20-minute range, indicating overextension by range-day momentum chasers)
rsi_60 < 25 (5-minute RSI confirms oversold — the downward micro-swing is mature and exhausting)
buy_ce.confirmation: Current 5s bar closes above its open (bullish reversal candle at the lower band). On NIFTY range days, the first green candle after touching the lower BB marks where buy-side market makers step in to absorb selling — this is the micro-inflection point.

conditions: close >= bb_upper_240 OR close within 3 spot points of bb_upper_240 (NIFTY has stretched to the upper edge of the range)
buy_pe.confirmation: Current 5s bar closes below its open (bearish reversal candle at the upper band)

exit.stop_rationale: On NIFTY range days, the overextension beyond the Bollinger Band typically doesn't exceed 15-20 spot points (7-10 option points) before reverting. A 5-point option stop allows for a further 10 spot point push against us — accommodating the common 'last gasp' pattern where aggressive momentum chasers push price slightly beyond the band before exhaustion. If the move exceeds this, the range day assumption is likely wrong — NIFTY is breaking out of its rotation, and the ADX will soon confirm a trend, invalidating the entire trade thesis.
exit.target_rationale: Range-day reversions on NIFTY from the BB edge toward VWAP/midline typically cover 20-40 spot points (10-20 option points) over 5-15 minutes. However, we target only the FIRST LEG of the reversion — the initial 15-20 spot points (8 option points) that occur in the first 60-90 seconds as market makers and mean-reversion algos drive price back from the extreme. Going for more than 8 points requires price to traverse the middle of the range where multiple participants compete and the move decelerates. This gives 1:1.6 risk-reward, consistent with the high win rate expected on confirmed range days (60%+).
exit.eod_rule: flatten at 14:15 — no trades in the last hour because range days can break out into trend into the close as institutional positioning for next day begins

filters.vix_filter: VIX between 12-22. Below 12, NIFTY's range days are too narrow (30-40 spot point range) for the BB bands to produce meaningful overextension signals — the moves are within noise. Above 22, range days are rare because elevated VIX implies event-driven volatility that creates trending sessions.
filters.time_filter: Session restricted to 10:15-14:15 IST. Before 10:15, the opening auction and first-hour volatility make ADX unreliable for range detection — the index needs 60+ minutes to establish whether the day is rotational. After 14:15, range days can break into trend as end-of-day positioning accelerates.
filters.volume_filter: Replaced by RSI oscillator — on NIFTY index, volume confirmation adds noise. The RSI extreme at the BB boundary serves the same purpose: confirming the micro-swing is exhausted.
filters.trend_filter: ADX < 18 IS the trend filter — this is the core mechanism. Additionally, the first-45-minute range check: if NIFTY's first 45 minutes produce a range greater than 1.8x the 14-minute ATR, the day is likely trending and the strategy stands down entirely.
filters.spread_filter: Skip if ATM option bid-ask > 2 points. Range-day environments typically have tight spreads due to lower volatility, so this filter also serves as a secondary range-day confirmation.

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — range-day mean-reversion is well-known, but the ADX gating on 5s NIFTY data with BB(2.2) precision bands provides differentiation from generic mean-reversion strategies

adaptation_notes: Six key adaptations from the original range_day_band_fade_003: (1) ADX lookback changed from 14 bars on 1-min (14 minutes) to 168 bars on 5s (14 minutes). This is a direct time-equivalence conversion because ADX measures trend strength over a time window, and 14 minutes is the correct window for detecting NIFTY intraday range regimes — it spans roughly one complete rotational swing leg. (2) Bollinger Band lookback changed from 20 bars on 1-min (20 minutes) to 240 bars on 5s (20 minutes). The 20-minute window captures the full half-period of NIFTY's range-day oscillation cycle, making the bands naturally align with the rotation boundaries. This is NOT a naive 12x scaling — the lookback is chosen to match the physical oscillation period. (3) MFI(5) replaced with RSI(60). The original used Money Flow Index because it was trading individual stocks where volume conviction matters. On NIFTY index, volume is aggregated across 50 constituents and doesn't cleanly signal directional conviction. RSI over 5 minutes (60 bars at 5s) provides the same overbought/oversold detection without volume noise. (4) VWAP slope window adjusted from 10 bars on 1-min (10 minutes) to 120 bars on 5s (10 minutes) — same time window, just rescaled for bar size. (5) Hold time compressed from 5-22 bars on 1-min (5-22 minutes) to 25-150 seconds. Range-day reversions on NIFTY start fast (first 30-60 seconds) and then slow dramatically as price approaches the midline. We capture the initial reversion impulse only. (6) Session windows retained exactly (10:15-14:15) because the logic is time-of-day dependent: range detection requires the opening period to establish the session structure, and late afternoon can break rotational regimes.
weaknesses: The strategy is entirely regime-dependent — if NIFTY transitions from range to trend mid-session (e.g., breaking news, sudden FII flow), band-touch entries become trend-continuation traps and the ADX filter may lag the transition by 2-5 minutes

NIFTY range days with very narrow ranges (sub-50 spot points) produce Bollinger Bands so tight that normal oscillation touches the 2.2x band, generating excess signals with shallow reversion potential — barely enough to cover the 4-point breakeven

ADX is inherently lagging — it confirms a range AFTER the range has been established, potentially missing the first few rotational swings of the session and only signaling when the best fades have already occurred

On BANKNIFTY weekly expiry days (Wednesdays), gamma hedging by options market makers creates artificial range-like behavior in the first half of the session that can suddenly break into violent trending moves as open interest clusters get hit

Multiple mean-reversion strategies competing at the same BB boundary during confirmed range days can create 'crowded fades' where everyone enters simultaneously, reducing fill quality and compressing the reversion magnitude
